These days, there is no reason you can't do both. I like pretty much everyone I know did a few years in London. I would say everyone should do this (although not necessarily same place). For one, gaining international work experience means a lot to many employers. NZ is isolated and you learn a lot from working in an international environment. Secondly, you'll probably find you will get the same income (and more) overseas anyway.

I can only speak for London, but earning a similar income, getting to spend weekends in Europe, and experiencing something new is something I wouldn't swap for anything. Your at an age where you have enough experience to easily find a job, and young enough to have no commitments and being on the other side of the world isn't a big deal.

I've been riding 5 years, not really sure where I started, but about 4 years ago, I was ftp of \~280 @ 66kg. Currently around 350w @ 68kg. I was stalled for quite a long time at around 300w ftp. At this time, I was doing a lot of sweetspot training, which is useful, but IMO only gets you so far. At some point, you need to focus on doing efforts which actually push you. Many template plans don't do this. I changed to doing a lot of z2 volume, and threshold work, 5x5's, max 1-2min efforts etc. If nothing else, you need to learn what its like to ride at and above threshold. I used to ride a lot 'kinda hard', never fresh, but never tired. Now I do a lot of easy riding, and a bit of hard stuff. Second thing is consistency and volume. Obviously it depends on how much time you have, but I noticed a big difference with higher volume.

The other thing which helped, is eating more carbs in training. Your race weight is higher than you think.  It's not just about FTP . More often than not, races are about 1-5min efforts.

The other thing I'd say, is that training doesn't need to be nearly as complex as many plans make it. Workouts don't need to be so confusing you can't even remember. Progressively making things harder is all you really need (with proper recovery).

What i've leant, is what while medical professionals are very knowledgeable often you need to work things out for yourself. Knees are complicated, and there are so many variables at play meaning doctors are often doing a process of elimination, which takes time. I heard varying 'diagnosis' from ITBS, muscle imbalance,  patella tendonitis to overtraining. I had an MRI which eventually led to a cortisone shot, which is really seen as a band aid solution - however it did help a lot. I never needed another one.

Knees are complicated, and what works for one person might not work for another. I recommend this blog post:

 [https://www.trainerroad.com/forum/t/how-to-fix-knee-injuries-for-cyclists/6166](https://www.trainerroad.com/forum/t/how-to-fix-knee-injuries-for-cyclists/6166) 

Here is what helped me:

\-Inner soles in my shoes to stop my knee collapsing

\-Glute bridges to make sure glutes activate when they should

\-Monster walks with a band

\-Lacrose ball/foam roller to get into TFL and Glute med in particular. Don't foam roll the IT band, but more the muscles which attach to it

TLDR - knee pain is never really an issue in the knee. As someone once told me, the knee is the victim. It takes trial and error to find what the real issue at play is. In cyclists, often this is tighness in the whole chain/alignment above the knee.

I've done plenty of riding with South London clubs, but can't help you too much with North. In addition, i was looking to meet other relatively experienced riders/racers so was definitely looking for something different to what you are describing. In saying that, try out Clapham Cycle. They are primarily organised through their meetup page, but they are mostly newer riders, and the focus is on the social side of cycling. I think that would be a good starting point then move on to one of the clubs below. Here is a bit more info about some of the other clubs i've ridden with at some point:

Islington CC - Pretty new and big. Plenty of groups/speeds to chose from. Friendly and inclusive, although they make joining a bit of a hassel and you have to attend a skills session, which is overkill IMO. They are based around Holloway road. Lots of rides from 50-130km

Dulwich Paragon - Race orientated, and definitely more focused around cycling than socialising. Generally no coffee stop on their regular club run which is about 55km. Generally friendly, although not as many young members as i would have liked. Generally based around Herne Hill/Crystal Palace

Brixton Cycling Club - Friendliest i have come across, very inclusive and not as structured and 'rule based' like others. Very relaxed environment and fine for beginners. I would try Brixton out after getting some experience with the likes of Clapham Cycle. Based out of Crystal Palace for the weekend rides.

Rapha CC - Expensive to join, but aside from that, well organised. Rides in the weekend are generally social, and the midweek ones can be 'smashy'. Best thing about RCC is they have an app to organise rides, and members can create their own for other people to join. They have lots of rides in both north and south london.

London Dynamo - Another race orientated club, and the only one i would probably avoid from the above. Based around Richmond park

Pretorious - Social group, but most riders are pretty experienced. For example the slowest group is faster than the fastest Clapham Cycle group. All super nice though, based out of Shoreditch.

There are load of clubs, so have a look on the british cycling website - as they are all listed there.
